Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of Day 2! The umpires and players walk out to the middle. Australian players spread out to their fielding positions after a small team huddle talk. The Indian opening pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul walks out to the crease. Mitchell Starc has the new Kookaburra cherry in his hands and will begin the proceedings with three slips in position. Off we go...
... THIRD INNINGS, DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Well then, a significant twist in this Test with the momentum slightly tilted toward the tourists, with the way they bowled throughout this day so far. Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna bagged three each while Jasprit Bumrah and Nitish Kumar Reddy both got two apiece. India's aim would be to replicate a similar performance with the bat when they come out in the final session. They have a thin lead of just 4 runs, and would want to bat throughout the post-Tea session, going unscathed. However, it is never going to be easy against the Aussie pace quad which will come at full tilt on a track that has fairly troubled the batters with its uneven bounce and skiddiness. A delicious third session is on the cards, folks! Stay tuned!

On the batting front, debutant Beau Webster showed remarkable composure, bringing up his maiden Test fifty in his very first match. His innings of 57 runs was characterized by smart cricket and unwavering focus. He found good support in Alex Carey, with the pair putting together a valuable 41-run stand before Prasidh Krishna struck again to break their partnership. With Bumrah still away for medical scans, the rest of India's bowling attack rose to the occasion. Nitish Kumar Reddy made a significant impact, picking up two quick wickets that saw Australia collapse from 162/6 to 166/9 with Prasidh too chipping in handy. And it did not take long for Siraj to snag the final wicket.

As the day progressed, the pitch began to show its teeth, with widening cracks and unpredictable bounce under the harsh sun. Steven Smith tried to weather the storm, finding an able partner in Beau Webster. The pair put together a fighting stand of 57 runs, showing good resistance until Prasidh Krishna broke through, dismissing Smith just before Lunch. Coming into the second session, and with Australia five down and still trailing, they desperately needed a solid partnership to first reduce the deficit and then build a lead. While Bumrah started the session, concern spread through the Indian camp as he left the field and was reportedly taken to the hospital for scans. In his absence, it was Virat Kohli who took the reigns.

After bundling out India for a modest total on day one, Australia's innings also got off to a rocky start when they lost Usman Khawaja during the tricky twilight period. Day two began with renewed energy from India's pace duo, as Bumrah struck early to remove Marnus Labuschagne. While Sam Konstas showed some courage with a few bold strokes, Siraj proved too hot to handle, picking up two quick wickets. With Travis Head's dismissal soon after, Australia found themselves reeling at 39/4.

TEA, DAY 2 - A clinical bowling performance from the Indians in this second session, and the tourists have now etched their names in both sessions played on Day 2! As it stands, this Test match hangs right in the balance with Australia and India both winning two apiece, along with a shared session. The absence of Jasprit Bumrah could have been a major setback, but India will be particularly satisfied with how the other seamers responded and operated. The performance of their third and fourth pace bowlers showed remarkable improvement. For Australia, from being 137/6, they stumbled down badly, getting blown up within the next 15 overs or so.

Rohit Sharma is in for a chat. Mentions that he has stepped down from this game but clarifies that he is not retiring or leaving the format. Shares that external opinions, whether from commentators, writers, or analysts, do not determine his decisions. Tells that he chose to stand down after arriving in Sydney, acknowledging that runs have not been coming off his bat. Further adds that there is no certainty that runs won't come in the future, whether in two months or five months. States that life changes every day and expresses full belief that things will improve in due time.

The pitch has certainly quickened up, which isn’t surprising with the sun beating down. From India's perspective, the key will be to pitch it up and allow the pitch to do the talking, rather than trying too hard to force wickets. As for Australia, it will be about rebuilding once again as they look to narrow the deficit. It's all set up for a crucial session, one that could give the Test its direction. The second session is set to commence at 7.40 am IST (2.10 am GMT). See you then. Cheers!

Jasprit Bumrah gave India an early breakthrough before Mohammed Siraj struck twice in quick succession, leaving Australia reeling at 39/4. Steven Smith faced a stern examination early in his innings but managed to shift the momentum with a six and a boundary off Prasidh Krishna. Those two strokes eased the pressure and took some sting out of India's early dominance. At the other end, Beau Webster complemented Smith by batting with positive intent to steady the ship. Just when it seemed like Australia would take the honours of the first session with their fightback in the second half, Prasidh Krishna managed to get Steven Smith to nick one, sending him back to the pavilion and pegging the hosts back.

SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs, 92 runs and 4 wickets. End of an entertaining session! It was a proper arm-wrestle, with India landing the first punch before Australia counterpunched. However, the tourists came back strong to land the final blow before the session ended, dismissing Steven Smith. India will go into the break with a slight edge, but both sides have had their moments, making for an intriguing contest.
